questionText: Solve the equation $\log_2(x + 3) + \log_2(x - 1) = 5$. Give all valid solutions, and show that any extraneous solutions are rejected.
markingScheme:
Combine logs: $\log_2((x+3)(x-1)) = 5$ **(1 mark)**
Convert to exponential form: $(x+3)(x-1) = 32$ **(1 mark)**
Expand and rearrange to $x^2 + 2x - 35 = 0$ **(1 mark)**
Solve: $x = 5$ or $x = -7$ **(1 mark)**
Check domain: reject $x = -7$ (makes $\log_2(x+3) = \log_2(-4)$ undefined) **(1 mark)**
State valid solution $x = 5$ **(1 mark)**

solutionSteps.step: Check the domain of the original equation
solutionSteps.explanation: $\log_2$ requires positive arguments, so $x + 3 > 0$ and $x - 1 > 0$, i.e. $x > 1$. Therefore $x = -7$ is rejected and the only valid solution is $x = 5$.
